items.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance
items.summary: Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI. Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.”
full_paragraphs: Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI.

Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.”

“Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”
Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS.

That said, users can disable this setting if they wish, which Whittaker said would “break our privacy guarantees.” She also admitted this is an “incomplete” solution, as it doesn’t “address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data.”

items.summary_pt: A Signal anunciou na sexta-feira que está limitando a capacidade dos usuários de fazer capturas de tela no aplicativo de mensagens seguro – uma resposta ao que a presidente Meredith Whittaker descreveu como a “ameaça existencial” dos sistemas operacionais que integram IA de agente. Whittaker escreveu que, ao dar aos agentes de IA a capacidade de “escanear” as informações nas telas dos usuários, Windows, Android e macOS/iOS “estão minando a capacidade do Signal de garantir a privacidade de forma independente”.
full_paragraphs_pt: A Signal anunciou na sexta-feira que está limitando a capacidade dos usuários de fazer capturas de tela no aplicativo de mensagens seguro – uma resposta ao que a presidente Meredith Whittaker descreveu como a “ameaça existencial” dos sistemas operacionais que integram IA de agente.

Whittaker escreveu que, ao dar aos agentes de IA a capacidade de “escanear” as informações nas telas dos usuários, Windows, Android e macOS/iOS “estão minando a capacidade do Signal de garantir a privacidade de forma independente”.

“Agora, a serviço dos recursos de agente de IA, seus dados confidenciais estão sendo capturados, armazenados e disponibilizados para qualquer banco de dados local ou servidor remoto que um agente de IA em nível de sistema operacional esteja usando naquele momento”, disse ela. “Tudo isso está fora do controle do Signal depois que os dados são capturados e coloca em risco a privacidade de todos os participantes de uma conversa.”
A Signal já procurou limitar esses riscos bloqueando capturas de tela de seu aplicativo do Windows por padrão. Agora está adicionando restrições semelhantes no Android e iOS.

Dito isso, os usuários podem desativar essa configuração se desejarem, o que Whittaker disse que “quebraria nossas garantias de privacidade”. Ela também admitiu que esta é uma solução “incompleta”, pois não “aborda outras maneiras mais sorrateiras pelas quais os agentes de IA poderiam acessar dados de aplicativos”.

items.title: A tale of two Nvidias
items.summary: We got two very different pictures of Nvidia this week, depending on whether you were focused on the company’s latest earnings report or the tech executives loudly calling for former CEO Jensen Huang’s return. On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Tim De Chant, and I discussed the latest news from the AI chipmaker, which reported soaring revenue and insisted that it has no plans for Huang to return.
full_paragraphs: We got two very different pictures of Nvidia this week, depending on whether you were focused on the company’s latest earnings report or the tech executives loudly calling for former CEO Jensen Huang’s return.

On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Tim De Chant, and I discussed the latest news from the AI chipmaker, which reported soaring revenue and insisted that it has no plans for Huang to return.

Kirsten described this as “the tale of two Nvidias this week,” with the company’s current executives assuring investors, “Hey, we’ve got this.” At the same time, “You’ve got Elon Musk and others out there really pushing to bring Jensen back, circulating a petition, Jensen himself saying that he’s prepared to come back.” (The company’s falling stock price certainly suggests that Wall Street isn’t feeling reassured.)
Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity.

Kirsten Korosec: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China. This was coming directly from the interim CEO Colette Kress, and that coincides with the Trump administration also talking about closing off what we have discussed in the past, which is this idea of remote access — really closing and tightening all these restrictions [so] the chips can’t make it into China.

What was happening is that data centers were being set up right outside, in countries like Malaysia and elsewhere, and then companies within China were remote accessing these chips, and so that’s now also been shut down.

A lot is happening on the China front that is so much bigger than Nvidia, but Nvidia came out publicly and said, “Nope, we’re shutting this part down.” I’ll be very curious to see if this changes, maybe in the first half of 2027.

Tim De Chant: I’d love to be a fly on the wall in some of these Trump administration conversations, because they were much more stringent in terms of export controls at the end of the first Trump administration, and that continued through the Biden administration, where they really restricted Nvidia’s ability to export chips to China. I think that something changed in the last couple of years that really opened Nvidia’s ability to sell in the country.

Kirsten Korosec: A Nvidia não venderá mais seus chips H200 na China. Isto veio diretamente da CEO interina Colette Kress, e isso coincide com o facto de a administração Trump também falar sobre encerrar o que discutimos no passado, que é esta ideia de acesso remoto – realmente fechar e reforçar todas estas restrições [para que] os chips não possam chegar à China.

O que estava a acontecer é que os centros de dados estavam a ser criados lá fora, em países como a Malásia e noutros lugares, e depois as empresas dentro da China estavam a aceder remotamente a estes chips, e agora eles também foram encerrados.

Muita coisa está acontecendo na frente da China que é muito maior do que a Nvidia, mas a Nvidia veio a público e disse: “Não, estamos encerrando esta parte”. Ficarei muito curioso para ver se isso muda, talvez no primeiro semestre de 2027.

Tim De Chant: Eu adoraria ser uma mosca na parede em algumas dessas conversas da administração Trump, porque elas eram muito mais rigorosas em termos de controles de exportação no final da primeira administração Trump, e isso continuou durante a administração Biden, onde eles realmente restringiram a capacidade da Nvidia de exportar chips para a China. Acho que algo mudou nos últimos anos que realmente abriu a capacidade da Nvidia de vender no país.

items.title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
items.summary: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
full_paragraphs: Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person.

You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later.
While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space.
Below are the most notable options so far, from general-purpose personal assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
Ask Proxy ’s biggest differentiator is that it “thinks like a woman,” meaning it aims to anticipate your needs before you even ask, the company explains on its website.

It works like a chatbot you can text like a friend, whether you need gift ideas, help planning an event, or recommendations for things to do that weekend. You can ask it to add important dates to your calendar, set reminders, or help with everyday decisions. You can also send it photos, like an empty table, to figure out how to decorate the table for a dinner party.

Unlike a typical chatbot, Ask Proxy also takes a proactive approach. It can reach out when it notices something you might forget or when it comes across a new activity, restaurant, or experience you might enjoy.
There’s also a work-focused version, which the company explains “gets employees back to work faster, while keeping personal data off company systems.”

Isso pode significar agendar um compromisso, organizar um calendário, pesquisar uma viagem, enviar um e-mail, fazer uma reserva, fazer compras online ou lembrá-lo de algo dias depois.

Embora o Instinct seja um dos agentes de IA mais badalados do momento, graças à sua avaliação de US$ 10 bilhões após sua última rodada de financiamento de US$ 1 bilhão, há muitos outros que também estão apostando neste espaço.
Abaixo estão as opções mais notáveis ​​até agora, desde assistentes pessoais de uso geral até agentes projetados para famílias, viagens e trabalho.
O maior diferencial do Ask Proxy é que ele “pensa como uma mulher”, o que significa que seu objetivo é antecipar suas necessidades antes mesmo de você perguntar, explica a empresa em seu site.

Funciona como um chatbot para o qual você pode enviar mensagens de texto como um amigo, se precisar de ideias para presentes, ajuda no planejamento de um evento ou recomendações de coisas para fazer naquele fim de semana. Você pode pedir para adicionar datas importantes ao seu calendário, definir lembretes ou ajudar nas decisões do dia a dia. Ao contrário de um chatbot típico, o Ask Proxy também adota uma abordagem proativa. Ele pode entrar em contato quando percebe algo que você pode esquecer ou quando se depara com uma nova atividade, restaurante ou experiência que você pode gostar.

full_paragraphs: Today, we’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows. Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline.

As a public benefit corporation, most of our work in pursuit of our mission takes place inside the company: research relevant to AI safety and interpretability; applied biomedical research; discounts on Claude for nonprofits and scientific institutions. These activities have both a public benefit component and for-profit value, so we house them directly in the company.

The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways: for example, we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.

One example is labor market impacts. AI may generate enormous economic value, but it could also cause instability for many workers. Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.

We’re establishing the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund as an LLC—rather than a 501(c)(3) or other format—to give adjustability between different forms of giving. None of the Anthropic equity held by the LLC will be used for lobbying or political giving, in the US or abroad.

Because of the way the Fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good. It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit.

This builds on commitments our co-founders and employees have already made. When Anthropic was founded, our co-founders pledged to donate 80% of their equity holdings, and since founding we have also operated an equity donation match program that allows employees to pledge equity which Anthropic matches. Approximately half of our employees participate in this program. When combined with today’s announcement, roughly 20% of Anthropic shares will be dedicated to the public good, plus any additional percentage that could be added if the company reaches specific valuation milestones.

In the coming months, we will share more about the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund’s structure and governance, including the valuation milestones that may add to its stake. We will also report on our progress to date against our mission in an upcoming public benefit report.
items.title_pt: Investir no benefício público
items.summary_pt: Hoje, estamos comprometendo parte das ações da Anthropic com o Fundo de Benefício Público da Anthropic, uma nova entidade integral com uma estrutura que aumenta a participação à medida que a empresa cresce. Sujeito à aprovação dos acionistas, 5% das ações da Anthropic serão comprometidas hoje, com 2% adicionais adicionados a critério do conselho para cada aumento de 50% no valor da empresa acima de uma linha de base definida. full_paragraphs_pt: Hoje, estamos comprometendo parte das ações da Anthropic com o Fundo de Benefício Público da Anthropic, uma nova entidade integral com uma estrutura que aumenta a participação à medida que a empresa cresce. Sujeito à aprovação dos acionistas, 5% das ações da Anthropic serão comprometidas hoje, com 2% adicionais adicionados a critério do conselho para cada aumento de 50% no valor da empresa acima de uma linha de base definida.

Como uma empresa de utilidade pública, a maior parte do nosso trabalho na prossecução da nossa missão ocorre dentro da empresa: investigação relevante para a segurança e interpretabilidade da IA; pesquisa biomédica aplicada; descontos em Claude para organizações sem fins lucrativos e instituições científicas. Estas atividades têm uma componente de benefício público e um valor lucrativo, pelo que as alojamos diretamente na empresa.

O Fundo Antrópico de Benefício Público terá maior flexibilidade e escala, permitindo-nos prosseguir a nossa missão de novas formas: por exemplo, poderemos explorar grandes doações para organizações sem fins lucrativos tradicionais ou distribuições diretas a populações específicas.

Um exemplo são os impactos no mercado de trabalho. A IA pode gerar um enorme valor económico, mas também pode causar instabilidade para muitos trabalhadores. A Anthropic já comprometeu 200 milhões de dólares para estudar e abordar esta questão, mas dado o ritmo do progresso da IA, poderão ser necessárias abordagens mais ousadas. O Fundo terá versatilidade para persegui-los.

Estamos estabelecendo o Fundo Antrópico de Benefício Público como uma LLC – em vez de um 501(c)(3) ou outro formato – para oferecer ajuste entre diferentes formas de doação. Nenhum patrimônio da Antrópico detido pela LLC será usado para lobby ou doações políticas, nos EUA ou no exterior.

Pela forma como o Fundo está estruturado, quanto mais a Antrópica cresce, maior é a parcela da empresa que pode ser dedicada expressamente ao bem público. É prática comum que as empresas de tecnologia ofereçam prêmios crescentes de remuneração aos seus executivos. Em vez disso, estamos direcionando essa equidade para o benefício público.

Isto se baseia em compromissos que nossos cofundadores e funcionários já assumiram. Quando a Anthropic foi fundada, nossos cofundadores se comprometeram a doar 80% de suas participações acionárias e, desde a fundação, também operamos um programa de equiparação de doações de ações que permite aos funcionários prometer ações equivalentes à Anthropic. Aproximadamente metade dos nossos funcionários participa deste programa. Quando combinado com o anúncio de hoje, cerca de 20% das ações da Anthropic serão dedicadas ao bem público, além de qualquer porcentagem adicional que possa ser adicionada se a empresa atingir marcos de avaliação específicos.

Nos próximos meses, compartilharemos mais sobre a estrutura e governança do Fundo Antrópico de Benefício Público, incluindo os marcos de avaliação que podem agregar à sua participação. Também informaremos sobre nosso progresso até o momento em relação à nossa missão em um próximo relatório de benefício público.

full_paragraphs: Today Anthropic, PBC announced the closing of its initial public offering of an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at a public offering price of $83.00 per share, including the full exercise by the underwriters of their option to purchase an additional 147,000,000 shares of Class A common stock from Anthropic at the initial public offering price. The offering consisted of 1,103,351,354 shares sold by Anthropic and 23,648,646 shares sold by certain selling stockholders. The aggregate gross proceeds from the offering, before deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and other offering expenses, were approximately $93.5 billion, of which approximately $91.6 billion was received by Anthropic. Anthropic did not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the selling stockholders.
Anthropic’s Class A common stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19, 2026 under the symbol “ANT.”

In addition to the shares of Class A common stock sold in the initial public offering, Anthropic closed the concurrent sale of an aggregate of 313,253,007 shares of Class N common stock to Advanced Micro Devices, Inc., Broadcom Inc., Google LLC, Micron Technology, Inc., Microsoft Corporation, NVIDIA Corporation, and TSMC Partners, Ltd. at the public offering price of $83.00 per share, in a private placement for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $26.0 billion. The sale of these shares of Class N common stock was not registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”). Aggregate gross proceeds from the initial public offering, including the shares sold by the selling stockholders, and the concurrent private placement were approximately $119.5 billion, before deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and other offering expenses.

Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC and Morgan Stanley acted as lead book-running managers for the offering. J.P. Morgan, Citigroup, Barclays, Wells Fargo Securities, BofA Securities, Deutsche Bank Securities, RBC Capital Markets, and UBS Investment Bank acted as book-running managers for the offering. BMO Capital Markets, BNP Paribas, Credit Agricole CIB, Jefferies, Mizuho, MUFG, and TD Securities acted as additional book-running managers for the offering. full_paragraphs: Qwen4-Max ranks 13th of 51 in our auto-annotation benchmark, first on wrist X-rays and second on retail shelves. Accuracy, cost and how to run it.

Alibaba released Qwen4-Max on November 16, 2026, calling it the most capable model in the Qwen family to date, with native vision and a one-million-token context window. We ran it through UL37, our 36-dataset detection benchmark, the same day.

Overall, Qwen4-Max ranks 13th of 51 models on our VLM Leaderboard, at 0.474 mAP 50 for $5.68 per 1,000 images. That average hides a sharper result. On pediatric wrist X-rays, it posts the highest score of any model we have tested, and it is second only to Gemini 4 Carbon on underwater scenes and densely packed retail shelves.

Qwen4-Max is now the Alibaba option for auto-annotation in Ultralytics Platform, replacing Qwen3.8-Max. Below is where it stands out, where it falls short, how it compares with the models you would weigh it against, and what a labeling batch costs.

UL37 measures how closely a model's boxes match human labels on 360 images: 10 from each of 36 real object detection datasets, from medical scans and aerial imagery to retail shelves, sports and circuit boards. Each dataset counts equally in the average, and every image goes through the same production pipeline Platform users get, with the dataset's own class names and SAM 3.1 refining each box, so the scores describe that refined pipeline rather than raw model output. The methodology is public.
UL37 results from the Ultralytics VLM Leaderboard, updated November 19, 2026. Qwen3.8-Max is no longer offered in Platform.

Qwen4-Max improves on Qwen3.8-Max on every headline metric, costs less per image and completed every benchmark request. It still sits well behind the leaders on average: GPT-6.1 Terra scores 0.560 for less money and in well under half the time.
Each dot is a paid model on the Ultralytics VLM Leaderboard.

full_paragraphs: GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra score 0.551 and 0.546 mAP 50 on 36 detection datasets, but Sol costs $8.10 per 1,000 images vs $31.88. Here's which to use.

OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol on November 17, 2026, describing Astra as its most capable model and Sol as its go-to model for everyday work. When we asked them to draw bounding boxes, their accuracy came out close. Their prices did not.

We ran both through UL37, our 36-dataset detection benchmark, the day they launched. GPT-6.2 Sol scored 0.551 mAP 50 and GPT-6.2 Astra 0.546, fourth and fifth of 50 models on our VLM Leaderboard. Sol did it for $8.10 per 1,000 images. Astra cost $31.88, almost four times as much.

Both are now the OpenAI Sol and Astra options for auto-annotation in Ultralytics Platform, replacing GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra. Below is how they compare, where each one leads, what a labeling batch costs, and when OpenAI's own GPT-6.1 Terra is still the better pick.

UL37 measures how closely a model's boxes match human labels on 360 images: 10 from each of 36 real object detection datasets, from medical scans and aerial imagery to retail shelves, sports, documents and circuit boards. The methodology is public.
UL37 results from the Ultralytics VLM Leaderboard, updated November 17, 2026.

In this run, the two are close on accuracy. Their mAP 50-95 scores, which reward tight boxes, differ by 0.001, and their precision by 0.003. Sol finds slightly more of the labeled objects: its 0.643 recall is the highest of all 50 models on the leaderboard, just ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon's 0.642. It is also the fastest of the top seven models, at 3.4 seconds per image.

full_paragraphs: Azure Custom Vision retires on September 25, 2028. Plan your migration, export your labeled data and retrain on Ultralytics Platform.

Azure Custom Vision retires on September 25, 2028. Teams that use its cloud training or prediction need a replacement before then, and teams running exported models will still want somewhere to retrain them as products and cameras change. It is a good moment to move to a platform you can keep labeling, training and deploying on for years.

This checklist walks through five steps that help a migration go smoothly: inventory what you run today, get your labeled data out, choose where to move, prove the new model on your own images, then switch over with a fallback. Along the way, it shows how each part of a Custom Vision project carries over to Ultralytics Platform, where you label, train and deploy Ultralytics YOLO models in one place, so the move gives your team a long-term home rather than a stopgap.

full_paragraphs: YOLO26n inference: 4.57 ms on a Jetson Orin Nano Super (TensorRT FP16) vs 67.03 ms on a Pi 5 CPU, in separate tests. Choose by model, FPS and cameras.

Should you run object detection on a Raspberry Pi 5 or an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano? For one camera, a low frame-rate target and a small model, a Pi 5 CPU can be enough: in our published benchmark, Ultralytics YOLO26n exported to NCNN takes 67.03 ms of inference per image on its four Arm cores, about 15 inference frames per second. When you need more cameras, a bigger model or more frame-rate headroom than your Pi delivers, a Jetson earns its place: on a Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit, the same model takes 4.57 ms as a TensorRT FP16 engine.

Ultralytics publishes this comparison and makes YOLO26, which runs on both boards; we don't make either board. Our Jetson numbers come from the Orin Nano Super Developer Kit, NVIDIA's entry-level Orin developer kit, and our Pi numbers from a Raspberry Pi 5, in separate tests. Many people still search for "Jetson Nano", the original 2019 board. It runs YOLO26 through JetPack 4, but our Jetson guide doesn't include YOLO26 benchmarks for it, so it appears here for specifications only.

Below: how the boards compare by model size, frame-rate target and number of camera streams, why FPS drops as you add cameras, how to measure both boards yourself, and which one fits your project. Setup steps live in the NVIDIA Jetson guide and the Raspberry Pi guide, and our walkthrough of object detection on a Raspberry Pi 5 CPU covers the Pi side in depth.

The boards solve the same problem with different silicon. The Raspberry Pi 5 is a general-purpose computer with four Arm Cortex-A76 cores and no dedicated AI accelerator, so our Pi benchmarks run YOLO on the CPU. The Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit pairs an Orin Nano module, built around an Ampere GPU, with a carrier board, and NVIDIA's TensorRT runtime compiles models for that GPU. It's an edge AI platform designed for this kind of workload.

Specifications, not measurements, checked November 19, 2026. NVIDIA's peak figures use different number formats, so they aren't directly comparable. The Orin Nano Super's 67 TOPS is a sparse INT8 figure; NVIDIA lists 33 TOPS dense. Jetson rows from the comparison and JetPack tables in the NVIDIA Jetson guide and the DeepStream guide; Pi 5 rows from the Raspberry Pi documentation.

Power is part of the choice too. NVIDIA lists the Orin Nano Super Developer Kit at 7 W to 25 W. When the board is flashed with a Super-enabled configuration, the Orin Nano 8GB offers 15 W, 25 W and MAXN SUPER power modes; with the default configuration it keeps its original 7 W and 15 W modes. Whichever board you pick, measure the whole system's draw with your cameras attached, since that's what your power supply and enclosure have to handle.

Price the whole build, not just the board: storage, power, cooling and cameras add up on both. Raspberry Pi has raised Pi 5 prices more than once in 2026 as memory costs climbed. As of November 2026 the 2GB Pi 5 lists at $77.50 and the 16GB board at $385. For current Jetson pricing and availability, check NVIDIA's developer kit page, and add the cost of any accelerator a Pi needs, such as the Raspberry Pi AI HAT+. For production, NVIDIA sells Jetson modules for your own carrier board; the developer kit we benchmarked is for development and prototyping.

Você deve executar a detecção de objetos em um Raspberry Pi 5 ou NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano? A Ultralytics publica essa comparação e faz o YOLO26, que roda em ambas as placas; não fazemos nenhuma das placas. Nossos números Jetson vêm do Orin Nano Super Developer Kit, do kit de desenvolvedor Orin básico da NVIDIA, e nossos números Pi de um Raspberry Pi 5, em testes separados. Muita gente ainda procura pela “Jetson Nano”, a placa original de 2019. Ele executa o YOLO26 até o JetPack 4, mas nosso guia Jetson não inclui benchmarks do YOLO26 para ele, portanto, aparece aqui apenas para especificações.

As etapas de configuração estão no guia NVIDIA Jetson e no guia Raspberry Pi, e nosso passo a passo de detecção de objetos em uma CPU Raspberry Pi 5 cobre o lado Pi em profundidade.

As placas resolvem o mesmo problema com silício diferente. O Raspberry Pi 5 é um computador de uso geral com quatro núcleos Arm Cortex-A76 e nenhum acelerador AI dedicado, portanto, nossos benchmarks Pi executam YOLO na CPU. O Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit emparelha um módulo Orin Nano, construído em torno de uma GPU Ampere, com uma placa transportadora, e o tempo de execução TensorRT da NVIDIA compila modelos para essa GPU. É uma plataforma de IA de ponta projetada para esse tipo de carga de trabalho.

Especificações, não medições, verificadas em 19 de novembro de 2026. Os números de pico da NVIDIA usam formatos numéricos diferentes, portanto, não são diretamente comparáveis. Qualquer que seja a placa que você escolher, meça o consumo de todo o sistema com as câmeras conectadas, pois é isso que a fonte de alimentação e o gabinete precisam lidar.

items.title: Is selling an AI version of your face to this microdrama startup the future of Hollywood?
items.summary: An actor has licensed his face to a microdrama startup — in a trend that's already popular in China. Experts question the long-term consequences if this becomes a trend in Hollywood, too.
full_paragraphs: For the most part, the content offered by the microdrama startup Shortical is indistinguishable from the rest of its industry. The company produces soapy, melodramatic storylines — almost always risqué romances — that, in bite-sized two-minute episodes, compel viewers to stay glued to their phones so as not to miss the latest twist in a tawdry, cliff-hanger-happy saga.

The primary way that Shortical — which was founded last January — makes money is through subscriptions. Typically, the first 7-10 episodes of a micro-drama are free. After that, if the user wants to finish the series, they have to pay a small monthly fee which unlocks access to all of the site’s content.

Over the past year, the company has churned out a gush of popular live-action romances like “Crossing the Line with My Neighbor,” “Accidentally Married My Boss,” and “Spoiled by My Billionaire Sugar Daddy.”

Lately, however, the company’s homepage is covered in AI-generated content. The reason isn’t exactly hard to figure out: the production overhead for AI content is substantially less than live-action. The profit potential, meanwhile, is substantially higher, if you can draw an audience.

Its latest microdrama premiered in Los Angeles last week. The series, called “Inevitable,” stars Aki Avni, an Israeli film and television star who has been visible in American TV shows for years (he had a stint on Fox’s 9/11-era thriller “24” years ago) but is now trying something largely unheard of in modern Hollywood: licensing his face to Shortical for the sake of its AI content.

The project, which is wholly AI, used Avni’s face to create a digital avatar of him. In “Inevitable,” he plays himself – in a very meta plot in which he — the actor Aki Avni — licenses his face to a film studio, after which thriller-like antics ensue.
This is Shortical’s first foray into such a licensing deal, but it likely won’t be their last.

In a phone interview, Avni told TechCrunch that he found the project both nerveracking and exciting. “Look, it’s a new era for artists,” the actor said. “AI is a new kind of art. It’s a new format. It’s always great to be the pioneer in something.”

full_paragraphs: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.

The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model.

Update, Nov 21: Posts on both Hacker News and X report that OpenRouter has sent customers an email notifying them that some of their prompts may have been read. OpenRouter cited the research and said that it received a report that the potential exposure involved prompts sent to MiniMax, a China-based model provider. OpenRouter said the researchers' planted URLs were accessed whether the prompts were sent to MiniMax directly or through three other resellers: AtlasCloud, Novita, and StreamLake. OpenRouter has removed a "Zero Data Retention" label from MiniMax-model endpoints. Hat tip: Sulat.com.

Muitos dos aplicativos de IA atuais usam serviços como OpenRouter ou Vercel que atuam como corretores. Esses “roteadores de IA”, às vezes também conhecidos como “gateways de IA”, recebem um grande número de prompts enviados de usuários finais de aplicativos de IA e os encaminham para um mecanismo de inferência disponível com base em critérios como aquele que cobra o preço mais baixo ou é o mais adequado para a tarefa determinada. Em vez de usar Anthropic, OpenAI ou outro grande fornecedor, o desenvolvedor contrata um roteador AI para encontrar o modelo mais adequado.

Para testar possíveis vazamentos, o pesquisador HD Moore reuniu uma coleção de chaves de acesso da Amazon Web Services, credenciais funcionais vinculadas a contas vazias da AWS, senhas para serviços como SSH e URLs exclusivos, nomes DNS e referências de repositórios git privados. Nenhum dos segredos havia sido usado antes e ele controlava a infraestrutura que recebia quaisquer solicitações usando as credenciais. Ele então semeou cada segredo em exatamente um prompt enviado a um único provedor. Caso algum dos segredos fosse divulgado, estes “canários” – assim chamados porque se assemelham ao papel daquela ave quando levado para as minas de carvão – permitiriam a Moore identificar cada elo da cadeia responsável.

full_paragraphs: Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a stealthy fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher who is taking a different approach to developing a fusion power plant.

The U.K.-based startup was founded in February, though sources told TechCrunch that the founder, Nantas Nardelli, has been working on the idea for longer. The people asked not to be identified because the information isn’t public. Bloomberg first reported Ek’s backing of Europa Fusion.

Nardelli has extensive experience in the AI world, having previously worked at Google DeepMind, Facebook AI Research, and Microsoft Research Cambridge. Recently, he was head of machine learning at Pacific Fusion, the fusion power startup based in Fremont, California.

Pacific Fusion recently broke ground on a demonstration facility in New Mexico. Like most fusion startups of its size, Pacific Fusion leans heavily on physical devices to test its theories and improve its simulations.

Nardelli apparently didn’t agree with the focus on hardware, instead thinking that fusion startups should invest in a more simulation- and data-heavy approach, a source familiar with his thinking told TechCrunch.

Like Pacific Fusion, Europa Fusion will pursue a pulsed-power approach to fusion. Pulsed-power reactors use massive, perfectly timed surges of electrical current to compress fuel targets until the atoms inside fuse and release energy.

Fusion power has the potential to be a significant energy source in the coming decades, but to date, no one has built a power plant capable of supplying electricity to the grid. If fusion power becomes commercially viable, though, it could possibly be a significant source of carbon-free power that draws on nearly limitless fuel supplies. The technology also has the potential to alleviate concerns about AI’s energy consumption.
Fusion’s ability to generate electricity without exacerbating climate change apparently drove Nardelli’s pivot from AI.

items.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
items.summary: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely…
full_paragraphs: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.

The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted, owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled.

The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. One of the biggest questions in AI right now is the extent to which progress on “verifiable” tasks—where it’s possible to check automatically whether an AI system has succeeded or failed—carry over into tasks on which success or failure is harder to measure. We know how to teach neural networks how to do verifiable tasks: Researchers have the systems attempt one many times, strengthen the neural pathways that contribute to success, and weaken the pathways that contribute to failures. That’s why AI systems have become so good at coding and math, two domains where it’s possible to determine automatically whether a solution does or doesn’t work.

It’s much harder to apply this technique, known as reinforcement learning, to tasks where success is less well defined or takes longer to ascertain—such as choosing a new research direction. For the same reason, it’s tough to evaluate AI performance on these tasks, so METR’s original time horizon plot didn’t include any of them. But it’s precisely this type of task that will prove essential if AI systems are to automate research and development.

And AI research and development is an especially hot topic right now. Parts of the AI community are still reeling from a different, heavily redacted METR report from earlier this month, which claimed that AI might be speeding up the pace of AI progress at Anthropic by a factor of two. That report sparked fears that the company (which just had a blockbuster IPO) could soon achieve full recursive self-improvement, a regime in which AI systems autonomously design their own successors with no human involvement.

METR researchers have worked to make sure their new suite of tasks includes some of the fuzzier, judgment-laden ones that could be most relevant to AI research and development. In one task, they ask models to design new AI evaluations that METR could use in its research and then have human METR employees score the results. Even though the most advanced models are now better than almost every human at software engineering, here they fall short: Not one of the AI-designed evaluations was good enough for METR employees to consider it useful for their research.

In another task, models have to score philosophical arguments. This task is intended to capture the extent to which models can exercise good judgment—though METR writes in the report that employees disagree about how relevant the task is for automation of AI R&D. On this task, too, models fell short of human performance.

Though it’s difficult to score these new tasks—and even harder to determine what the scores mean—experts I spoke with appreciate that METR is incorporating new types of evaluations into its work. “We’re at the point where AI evaluations need to get more creative,” says Sayash Kapoor, a computer scientist and incoming professor at UC Berkeley. “Trying to push the envelope of the space of evaluations is a welcome change.”
items.title_pt: O gráfico mais incompreendido em IA acaba de receber uma grande atualização
items.summary_pt: Um novo relatório da organização sem fins lucrativos de avaliação de IA METR conclui que algumas capacidades de IA continuam a melhorar ao longo de uma trajetória exponencial – mas também indica que os modelos não são tão bons em tarefas que exigem julgamento como são na codificação. O relatório é uma atualização do gráfico do horizonte temporal da organização, que foi amplamente…
full_paragraphs_pt: Um novo relatório da organização sem fins lucrativos de avaliação de IA METR conclui que algumas capacidades de IA continuam a melhorar ao longo de uma trajetória exponencial – mas também indica que os modelos não são tão bons em tarefas que exigem julgamento como são na codificação.

O relatório é uma atualização do gráfico do horizonte temporal da organização, que foi amplamente partilhado – e amplamente mal interpretado, devido à complexidade das medidas utilizadas. O METR avaliou os modelos fazendo-os tentar um grande conjunto de tarefas, cada uma das quais também concluída por humanos. A dificuldade de cada tarefa foi pontuada de acordo com o tempo que os testadores humanos levaram para concluí-la – e então os modelos foram classificados de acordo com a duração das tarefas que conseguiram concluir. Esse gráfico mostrou que os sistemas de IA estavam a melhorar rapidamente – a cada quatro meses, a duração das tarefas que os modelos de fronteira conseguiam completar com sucesso duplicava.

O enredo atualizado adiciona mais tarefas – algumas que estimam que levam muito mais tempo para os humanos do que aquelas do conjunto original e outras que são mais abertas. Uma das maiores questões da IA ​​neste momento é até que ponto o progresso em tarefas “verificáveis” – onde é possível verificar automaticamente se um sistema de IA foi bem-sucedido ou falhou – é transferido para tarefas nas quais o sucesso ou o fracasso são mais difíceis de medir. Sabemos como ensinar as redes neurais a realizar tarefas verificáveis: os pesquisadores fazem com que os sistemas tentem uma tarefa muitas vezes, fortalecendo os caminhos neurais que contribuem para o sucesso e enfraquecendo os caminhos que contribuem para o fracasso. É por isso que os sistemas de IA se tornaram tão bons em codificação e matemática, dois domínios onde é possível determinar automaticamente se uma solução funciona ou não.

É muito mais difícil aplicar esta técnica, conhecida como aprendizagem por reforço, a tarefas onde o sucesso é menos bem definido ou demora mais tempo a ser determinado – como a escolha de uma nova direção de investigação. Pela mesma razão, é difícil avaliar o desempenho da IA ​​nessas tarefas, então o gráfico de horizonte de tempo original do METR não incluía nenhuma delas. Mas é precisamente este tipo de tarefa que se revelará essencial para que os sistemas de IA possam automatizar a investigação e o desenvolvimento.

E a pesquisa e o desenvolvimento de IA são um tema especialmente importante no momento. Partes da comunidade de IA ainda estão se recuperando de um relatório METR diferente e fortemente redigido do início deste mês, que afirmava que a IA poderia estar acelerando o ritmo do progresso da IA ​​na Antrópica por um fator de dois. Esse relatório despertou receios de que a empresa (que acaba de realizar uma IPO de grande sucesso) possa em breve alcançar o auto-aperfeiçoamento recursivo completo, um regime em que os sistemas de IA concebem autonomamente os seus próprios sucessores, sem envolvimento humano.

Os pesquisadores do METR têm trabalhado para garantir que seu novo conjunto de tarefas inclua algumas das tarefas mais confusas e carregadas de julgamento que poderiam ser mais relevantes para a pesquisa e desenvolvimento de IA. Em uma tarefa, eles pedem aos modelos que projetem novas avaliações de IA que o METR possa usar em suas pesquisas e, em seguida, fazem com que funcionários humanos do METR classifiquem os resultados. Embora os modelos mais avançados sejam agora melhores do que quase todos os seres humanos em engenharia de software, aqui eles ficam aquém: nenhuma das avaliações concebidas pela IA foi suficientemente boa para que os funcionários do METR a considerassem útil para a sua investigação.

Numa outra tarefa, os modelos têm de pontuar argumentos filosóficos. Esta tarefa destina-se a captar até que ponto os modelos podem exercer o bom senso – embora o METR escreva no relatório que os funcionários discordam sobre a relevância da tarefa para a automação da I&D de IA. Também nesta tarefa os modelos ficaram aquém do desempenho humano.

Embora seja difícil pontuar estas novas tarefas – e ainda mais difícil determinar o significado das pontuações – os especialistas com quem falei apreciam o facto de o METR estar a incorporar novos tipos de avaliações no seu trabalho. “Estamos no ponto em que as avaliações de IA precisam ser mais criativas”, diz Sayash Kapoor, cientista da computação e professor iniciante na UC Berkeley. “Tentar ampliar o espaço das avaliações é uma mudança bem-vinda.”

items.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
items.summary: OpenAI’s layered approach to adversarial distillation combines model training, safeguards, detection, and enforcement to protect against capability extraction.
full_paragraphs: How we’re addressing safety risks of distillation and lessons we’ve learned for strengthening safeguards across the industry.

As frontier AI models become more capable, safeguards play an increasingly important role in how they can be used responsibly. Adversarial distillation creates a path for bad actors to reproduce these capabilities without appropriate safeguards. An actor may use a frontier model’s outputs without authorization to train another model with similar capabilities, then deploy it without comparable protections. For instance, an adversary might distill a model’s cyber capabilities and use the resulting model to help carry out cyberattacks that the original model would have refused to assist with or that its safeguards would have blocked.

We’re sharing how OpenAI detects and disrupts adversarial distillation, how we’ve strengthened protections for our models’ protected reasoning, and what we’ve learned that can help strengthen defenses across the industry.

Our approach to adversarial distillation combines adversarial testing, model training, classifiers, and API-level protections with investigations into coordinated attempts to extract model capabilities. These updated safeguards align more closely with those we use for biology and cybersecurity.

We place particular emphasis on preventing attackers from extracting our models’ protected reasoning: the intermediate steps a model generates internally while working toward an answer, known as its chain-of-thought. These traces can contain information the final answer leaves out, making them especially valuable training data for another model.

W e’ve strengthened our defenses against protected reasoning extraction in GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol. In an internal adaptive evaluation using strong automated red-teaming, we tested whether attackers could recover protected reasoning the model had generated while answering an earlier prompt. The average attack success rate fell from 54.0% against GPT‑6 Astra with its original safeguards to 0.2% against GPT‑6.2 Astra with its updated safeguards.

Distillation is a common machine-learning technique in which one model learns from data produced by another. For example, a model can learn from another model’s answers, its reasoning, or its judgments about which answers are better and why. Beyond intellectual property concerns, unauthorized distillation poses serious safety risks. Through adversarial distillation, a second model can learn advanced frontier capabilities without inheriting the safeguards that govern how the original model can use them.

The concern is especially clear in dual-use domains like cybersecurity and biology. A model that helps defenders find vulnerabilities in software could also help an attacker exploit them; a model that assists with biological research could also help someone develop a harmful pathogen. If such capabilities were transferred to a model with weaker safeguards, it may provide assistance that the original model would have refused, or that the original safeguards would have blocked.
items.title_pt: Combatendo a destilação adversária
items.summary_pt: A abordagem em camadas da OpenAI para destilação adversária combina treinamento de modelo, salvaguardas, detecção e fiscalização para proteção contra extração de capacidade.
full_paragraphs_pt: Como estamos abordando os riscos de segurança da destilação e as lições que aprendemos para fortalecer as salvaguardas em toda a indústria.

À medida que os modelos de IA de fronteira se tornam mais capazes, as salvaguardas desempenham um papel cada vez mais importante na forma como podem ser utilizadas de forma responsável. A destilação adversária cria um caminho para que os malfeitores reproduzam essas capacidades sem as salvaguardas adequadas. Um ator pode usar os resultados de um modelo de fronteira sem autorização para treinar outro modelo com capacidades semelhantes e, em seguida, implantá-lo sem proteções comparáveis. Por exemplo, um adversário pode destilar as capacidades cibernéticas de um modelo e utilizar o modelo resultante para ajudar a realizar ataques cibernéticos que o modelo original teria recusado ajudar ou que as suas salvaguardas teriam bloqueado.

Estamos compartilhando como a OpenAI detecta e interrompe a destilação adversária, como fortalecemos as proteções para o raciocínio protegido de nossos modelos e o que aprendemos que pode ajudar a fortalecer as defesas em todo o setor.

Nossa abordagem à destilação adversária combina testes adversários, treinamento de modelo, classificadores e proteções em nível de API com investigações sobre tentativas coordenadas de extrair recursos de modelo. Estas salvaguardas atualizadas alinham-se mais estreitamente com aquelas que usamos para biologia e segurança cibernética.

Colocamos ênfase especial em impedir que invasores extraiam o raciocínio protegido de nossos modelos: as etapas intermediárias que um modelo gera internamente enquanto trabalha em direção a uma resposta, conhecidas como cadeia de pensamento. Esses rastreamentos podem conter informações que a resposta final deixa de fora, tornando-os dados de treinamento especialmente valiosos para outro modelo.

Reforçamos nossas defesas contra a extração de raciocínio protegido no GPT‑6.2 Astra e no GPT‑6.2 Sol. Em uma avaliação adaptativa interna usando red-teaming automatizado forte, testamos se os invasores poderiam recuperar o raciocínio protegido que o modelo havia gerado ao responder a um prompt anterior. A taxa média de sucesso de ataque caiu de 54,0% contra o GPT‑6 Astra com suas salvaguardas originais para 0,2% contra o GPT‑6.2 Astra com suas salvaguardas atualizadas.

A destilação é uma técnica comum de aprendizado de máquina na qual um modelo aprende com os dados produzidos por outro. Por exemplo, um modelo pode aprender com as respostas de outro modelo, com o seu raciocínio ou com os seus julgamentos sobre quais respostas são melhores e porquê. Além das preocupações com a propriedade intelectual, a destilação não autorizada representa sérios riscos de segurança. Através da destilação adversária, um segundo modelo pode aprender capacidades avançadas de fronteira sem herdar as salvaguardas que regem a forma como o modelo original pode utilizá-las.

A preocupação é especialmente clara em domínios de dupla utilização, como a cibersegurança e a biologia. Um modelo que ajude os defensores a encontrar vulnerabilidades no software também poderia ajudar um invasor a explorá-las; um modelo que auxilie na pesquisa biológica também poderia ajudar alguém a desenvolver um patógeno prejudicial. Se essas capacidades fossem transferidas para um modelo com salvaguardas mais fracas, poderia fornecer uma assistência que o modelo original teria recusado ou que as salvaguardas originais teriam bloqueado.

items.title: Can AI help scientists identify promising drug candidates?
items.summary: MedChemBench evaluates how well AI models interpret molecular structures, reason from experimental evidence, and select compounds in early drug discovery.
full_paragraphs: Introducing MedChemBench, a benchmark that tests how well AI models read molecular structures, interpret experimental results, and choose which compounds to test next.

We’re introducing MedChemBench, a benchmark that evaluates AI models on reasoning tasks drawn from medicinal chemistry research. It tests whether models can connect a molecule’s structure with experimental evidence to explain results, compare compounds, and predict their properties. Building AI that can reliably support this work is one step towards helping scientists develop better medicines.

One of the hardest parts of this work is that improving one property of a molecule can make another worse. A compound might act strongly against a disease related protein but be poorly absorbed or break down too quickly in the body. Medicinal chemists work through these tradeoffs by designing, making, and testing related compounds, then deciding what to try next. For AI to help, it needs to connect changes in molecular structure with experimental evidence and reason about what compounds are worth pursuing.

MedChemBench measures these abilities through 99 problems drawn from published research. At the xhigh reasoning setting, GPT‑6.2 Astra earned 84.5% of the available credit, compared with 83.3% for GPT‑6 Astra, 82.0% for GPT‑6.1 Sol, and 58.2% for GPT‑5.6 Sol. GPT‑6 Astra was strongest at reconstructing molecular structures and explaining experimental evidence. Selecting compounds and predicting their numerical properties proved harder for that model.

MedChemBench draws on 117 papers and patents and includes 761 distinct molecular structures. For most problems, models receive the context available at a chosen point in a research program: the biological target, the researchers’ goals, the compounds studied so far, and selected experimental findings.
Molecular structures. Correct atom connections and specified stereochemistry in molecules assembled from the drawings and chemical groups provided.
Scientific reasoning. Explanations supported by the supplied evidence, such as the reasons for choosing one compound over another.
Ranking and selection. Compound rankings and choices that meet the stated requirements.
items.title_pt: A IA pode ajudar os cientistas a identificar candidatos promissores a medicamentos?
items.summary_pt: O MedChemBench avalia quão bem os modelos de IA interpretam as estruturas moleculares, raciocinam a partir de evidências experimentais e selecionam compostos na descoberta inicial de medicamentos.
full_paragraphs_pt: Apresentando o MedChemBench, um benchmark que testa quão bem os modelos de IA leem estruturas moleculares, interpretam resultados experimentais e escolhem quais compostos testar em seguida.

Estamos apresentando o MedChemBench, um benchmark que avalia modelos de IA em tarefas de raciocínio extraídas de pesquisas em química medicinal. Ele testa se os modelos podem conectar a estrutura de uma molécula com evidências experimentais para explicar resultados, comparar compostos e prever suas propriedades. Construir uma IA que possa apoiar este trabalho de forma confiável é um passo para ajudar os cientistas a desenvolver medicamentos melhores.

Uma das partes mais difíceis deste trabalho é que melhorar uma propriedade de uma molécula pode piorar outra. Um composto pode agir fortemente contra uma proteína relacionada a uma doença, mas ser mal absorvido ou decompor-se muito rapidamente no corpo. Os químicos medicinais resolvem essas compensações projetando, fabricando e testando compostos relacionados e, em seguida, decidindo o que tentar em seguida. Para que a IA ajude, ela precisa conectar as mudanças na estrutura molecular com evidências experimentais e raciocinar sobre quais compostos valem a pena buscar.

O MedChemBench mede essas habilidades por meio de 99 problemas extraídos de pesquisas publicadas. Na configuração de raciocínio xhigh, o GPT‑6.2 Astra obteve 84,5% do crédito disponível, em comparação com 83,3% para o GPT‑6 Astra, 82,0% para o GPT‑6.1 Sol e 58,2% para o GPT‑5.6 Sol. O GPT‑6 Astra foi mais forte na reconstrução de estruturas moleculares e na explicação de evidências experimentais. Selecionar compostos e prever suas propriedades numéricas mostrou-se mais difícil para esse modelo.

MedChemBench baseia-se em 117 artigos e patentes e inclui 761 estruturas moleculares distintas. Para a maioria dos problemas, os modelos recebem o contexto disponível num ponto escolhido num programa de investigação: o alvo biológico, os objetivos dos investigadores, os compostos estudados até agora e resultados experimentais selecionados.

Raciocínio científico. Explicações apoiadas pelas evidências fornecidas, tais como as razões para a escolha de um composto em detrimento de outro.

Chess.com is ready to go a lot bigger than chess. After launching Gambit, a gambling-free poker site, earlier this year, the company is now adding 10 more games: backgammon, checkers, go, hearts, mahjong, shogi, sudoku, solitaire, xiangqi, and a Scrabble alternative called word. They’re all part of Chess’s new Classic Games platform, which is launching its public beta on Saturday on the web and through a new app for iOS and Android.

“Our cofounders have had many people come up to them and say, ‘Hey, I run a mahjong night on Wednesdays’ or ‘I go to this local bar in Chicago with like five people, and we love playing go, but we lack a Chess.com,’” chief growth officer Albert Cheng says in an interview with The Verge. “The way that Chess.com has grown this community of almost 300 million members has not really happened for a lot of these other types of classic games.”

Classic Games is aimed at filling that gap. Some of the new games, like shoji or xiangqi, are strategy games similar to chess while others are further afield, like sudoku, solitaire, and word. The Classic team chose the new games through “a mix of community feedback, market research, and then just our own confidence in our ability to serve that game well,” Cheng says. It’s focused on classics that “have some sort of lifelong journey of learning and a community.”

Classic Games will feel familiar if you’ve ever played a match on Chess.com. Each game has lessons, leaderboards, and a rating system. Multiplayer games like checkers or mahjong have options for matches against other players or bots, and they use the same bot characters that Chess.com has. (Martin remains the lowest-rated bot across the board, whether it’s on Chess, Gambit, or Classic.) Not all of the games have the same play modes — word and mahjong have puzzles like chess, while sudoku has a set of daily grids and solitaire has daily deals.

full_paragraphs: A Russian national has been indicted on suspicions he was a Russian spy who stalked and surveilled employees of a Silicon Valley company that was assisting Ukraine in its ongoing war with its eastern neighbor.

Igor D’iu, 25, allegedly photographed the employees and their computer screens as they worked at a coffee shop located near the company’s Palo Alto office, federal prosecutors said Wednesday. He also kept a list of home addresses of employees and a senior executive. At one point, prosecutors said, D’iu trailed an employee as she traveled home from Palo Alto to San Francisco. An affidavit filed in the case referred to the employee as FEMP1, short for female employee, and said the event left her “in a state of emotional distress.”

“FEMP1 made evasive and irregular turns, took back roads, and turned into a grocery store parking lot where D’IU continued aggressively following her vehicle,” an FBI special agent wrote. “D’IU followed FEMP1 through U-turns, illegal left turns, and ran a red light to stay with FEMP1 for nearly thirty miles. FEMP1 called 911 while driving and was instructed to drive directly to San Francisco Police Department (“SFPD”) Mission Station. Near SFPD Mission Station, FEMP1 flagged an SFPD patrol vehicle and reported the incident. D’IU left once FEMP1 made contact with the patrol vehicle.”

full_paragraphs: NVIDIA and Microsoft are extending their full-stack collaboration to help organizations build, customize and deploy intelligent applications — from next-generation infrastructure on Azure to industrial systems and Windows PCs.

At Microsoft Ignite, the companies are expanding access to Azure virtual machines powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, as well as adding customer availability to NVIDIA open models and customization capabilities through Microsoft Foundry, and new options for running AI at the edge, where businesses generate and use their data.

Microsoft is also using NVIDIA technologies to accelerate its own models and services, including NVIDIA Dynamo inference software for post-training and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs for Bing search models.
NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are running in Azure data centers, providing infrastructure designed for demanding reasoning, agentic applications, and large-scale model training and inference.

Microsoft and NVIDIA are also collaborating to extend confidential computing to bare-metal and rack-scale AI infrastructure. The work will help protect sensitive models and data while they are being processed, supporting organizations that need to work with proprietary or regulated information.

NVIDIA Confidential Computing and attestation help customers verify the computing environment before releasing sensitive models, data or keys. As AI workloads span more interconnected accelerators, the companies are working to extend those protections across the AI factory infrastructure.
To help data centers get more performance from available power, NVIDIA and Microsoft are also collaborating on power efficiency using NVIDIA MaxLPS.

Azure’s Vera Rubin preview builds on NVIDIA and Microsoft’s codesign and performance optimization, underscored in the latest NVIDIA Blackwell-based MLPerf results. In MLPerf Training v6.1, Azure scaled to 10,240 NVIDIA GPUs with GB200 NVL72 systems on the DeepSeek-V3 model, the largest scale in the round. In MLPerf Inference v6.1, Azure’s NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems led cloud submissions on DeepSeek-R1 interactive throughput by over 10%, per Signal65.

full_paragraphs: Tool Retrieval is now in preview in the Gemini Interactions API. Load tool parameter schemas on demand instead of sending your full tool library in every prompt,designed to reduce input tokens and keep tool selection accurate as your agent scales.

We are launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API to help your agents manage large tool libraries more efficiently. By loading parameter schemas only when needed, you reduce latency and input token costs for complex tasks. You can try this feature today in the Interactions API by adding a tool_search tool and setting defer_loading to true in your requests.

We are introducing Tool Retrieval to help developers manage large collections of software tools more efficiently. Instead of loading every tool at once, your agent now keeps a library on standby and only pulls in the specific details it needs for a task. This reduces data usage, speeds up performance, and improves accuracy. You can start using this feature today with our latest Gemini models to build more capable and responsive applications.
Today we're launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API, available in preview in the Interactions API.

When an agent connects to dozens or even hundreds of tools, sending every full parameter schema on every request adds up fast. It inflates input token counts, adds latency, and lowers tool-selection accuracy as the candidate list grows. Tool Retrieval lets your agent keep its full tool library on standby and load parameter schemas only when the current task needs them.

To turn on Tool Retrieval, add a tool_search tool to your request and set defer_loading: true on the tools you want to hold back. The model still sees the name and description of every deferred tool, so it knows what's available, but the parameter schemas stay out of context. When the model needs a tool, it asks for it by name, the API loads the full schema, and the model calls the function, all inside the same request.

from google import genai client = genai.Client() tools = [ {"type": "tool_search"}, { "type": "function", "name": "issue_refund", "description": "Refund an order to the original payment method.", "defer_loading": True, "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_id": {"type": "string"}, "amount": {"type": "number"}, }, "required": ["order_id", "amount"], }, }, #... 50+ other deferred functions (leave frequent tools undeferred) ] interaction = client.interactions.create( model="gemini-4-hydrogen", input="Order A-1042 arrived damaged. Please refund 40 dollars.", tools=tools, ) Inside that single API call, the model searches for issue_refund, the API loads its schema, and the model emits the function_call. All three steps appear in interaction.steps, making it easy to inspect which tools the model considered when debugging tool names or descriptions:

"steps": [ { "type": "tool_search_call", "id": "tsc_7f2a", "arguments": {"function_names": ["issue_refund"]}, "signature": "..." }, { "type": "tool_search_result", "call_id": "tsc_7f2a", "result": [{"type": "function", "name": "issue_refund", "parameters": {...}}], "signature": "..." }, { "type": "function_call", "id": "fc_91c3", "name": "issue_refund", "arguments": {"order_id": "A-1042", "amount": 40} } ] From here it's normal function calling: your code runs the refund and sends back a function_result.

Estamos introduzindo o Tool Retrieval para ajudar os desenvolvedores a gerenciar grandes coleções de ferramentas de software com mais eficiência. Em vez de carregar todas as ferramentas de uma vez, seu agente agora mantém uma biblioteca em espera e extrai apenas os detalhes específicos necessários para uma tarefa. Isso reduz o uso de dados, acelera o desempenho e melhora a precisão. Você pode começar a usar esse recurso hoje mesmo com nossos modelos Gemini mais recentes para criar aplicativos mais capazes e responsivos.
Hoje estamos lançando o Tool Retrieval na API Gemini, disponível em versão prévia na API Interactions.

Quando um agente se conecta a dezenas ou até centenas de ferramentas, o envio de todos os esquemas de parâmetros completos em cada solicitação aumenta rapidamente. Ele aumenta a contagem de tokens de entrada, adiciona latência e reduz a precisão da seleção de ferramentas à medida que a lista de candidatos aumenta. A recuperação de ferramentas permite que seu agente mantenha sua biblioteca completa de ferramentas em espera e carregue esquemas de parâmetros somente quando a tarefa atual precisar deles.

Para ativar a recuperação de ferramentas, adicione uma ferramenta tool_search à sua solicitação e defina defer_loading: true nas ferramentas que você deseja reter. O modelo ainda vê o nome e a descrição de cada ferramenta adiada, portanto sabe o que está disponível, mas os esquemas de parâmetros permanecem fora do contexto. Quando o modelo precisa de uma ferramenta, ele a solicita pelo nome, a API carrega o esquema completo e o modelo chama a função, tudo dentro da mesma solicitação.

from google import genai client = genai.Client() tools = [ {"type": "tool_search"}, { "type": "function", "name": "issue_refund", "description": "Reembolsar um pedido para o método de pagamento original.", "defer_loading": True, "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_id": {"type": "string"}, "amount": {"type": "number"}, }, "required": ["order_id", "amount"], }, }, #... 50+ outras funções adiadas (deixe ferramentas frequentes indeferidas) ] interação = client.interactions.create( model="gemini-4-hydrogen", input="O pedido A-1042 chegou danificado. Por favor, devolva 40 dólares.", tools=tools, ) Dentro dessa única chamada de API, o modelo procura por issue_refund, a API carrega seu esquema e o modelo emite a function_call. Todas as três etapas aparecem em interact.steps, facilitando a inspeção de quais ferramentas o modelo considerou ao depurar nomes ou descrições de ferramentas:

"etapas": [ { "tipo": "tool_search_call", "id": "tsc_7f2a", "argumentos": {"function_names": ["issue_refund"]}, "signature": "..." }, { "type": "tool_search_result", "call_id": "tsc_7f2a", "resultado": [{"type": "função", "nome": "issue_refund", "parameters": {...}}], "signature": "..." }, { "type": "function_call", "id": "fc_91c3", "name": "issue_refund", "arguments": {"order_id": "A-1042", "amount": 40} } ] A partir daqui é uma chamada de função normal: seu código executa o reembolso e envia de volta um function_result.

full_paragraphs: Over the past week, anyone could be forgiven for wondering whether a Diehard IV –style cyberwar had finally arrived in the US.

Across just four consecutive business days, a mass Microsoft exchange outage broke IT services for thousands of companies, a Federal Aviation Administration tech screw-up grounded airplanes across the country, a software problem affecting JPMorgan Chase caused another round of disruption, a United Airlines system glitch delayed flights yet again, and an NSA classified network’s downtime left the agency’s staff sitting at home waiting to return to their office at Fort Meade. In the midst of a US war with Iran and rising fears of AI-enabled hacking, this still-unfolding comedy of IT errors colliding across American infrastructure felt to plenty of observers like more than a coincidence.

Yet there’s still no evidence that any one of these clustered technological failures were related, much less caused by hackers. Their improbable, sequential timing left Americans anxiously doomscrolling for signs of foul play. But in cases like these, it’s the job of cybersecurity analysts (and reporters at WIRED) to determine—vibes aside—whether the latest tech outage was actually an accident or the result of a cyberattack.

full_paragraphs: Good morning, and welcome to our 12,783 new readers. Google spent most of 2026 being mocked for moving slowly. But something changed this fall, and it’s now shipping faster than ever. Maybe the key is, as Demis Hassabis put it, “alchemy at its finest.”

The company’s new Neon model is the latest step up both the periodic table and the leaderboard, carrying a mid-tier label but with scores nearing the industry’s best. With one researcher hinting at self-improving AI behind the pace, Google suddenly feels very, very back.

The Rundown: Google just released Gemini 4 Neon, a faster sibling to its top-end Carbon that leads Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Sol on most of Google’s tests — marking the company’s fourth Gemini 4 model in under two months.

Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks.

RTX Spark desktops are equipped with a 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU, an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores and up to 128GB of unified memory, delivering up to 1 petaflop of AI performance. Ten-gigabit Ethernet connectivity enables fast transfers of large datasets, model files and creative assets between RTX Spark compact desktops and networked storage.

items.title: This smell startup says its AI nose is as good as a human’s
items.summary: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation…
full_paragraphs: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The company’s goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.”

“Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.”

In the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating between smells, and about as good as a junior perfume designer at creating them. It says its technology is already being used in the fragrance industry to help brands design and manufacture new scents. Last month, the company says, Osmo’s AI model outperformed in-house perfumers at one of the world’s largest consumer goods companies. Wiltschko believes it could be deployed eventually for threat detection at airports, for example, or diagnosing diseases.

Wiltschko spun the startup out of his work at Google Brain, the search giant’s former AI research lab, in 2023, and he is running the same playbook as AI startups in other domains: Throw a lot of data at difficult problems, and see what happens. The challenge with scent, Wiltschko says, is that there was a dearth of good data. Before Osmo, there were fewer than 200,000 human descriptions of smells in existing databases, by his count. Plus, the chemical sensor devices needed to collect data are expensive, and the fragrance industry is secretive about its work on olfactory science.

A lot of the company’s work has been in creating its own dataset of more than 10 million human labels and 800 million “scent tokens,” which describe the exact molecules and concentrations that go into creating specific odors. Osmo uses spectrometers and other chemical sensors, running around the clock, to break down the molecular makeup of everything from fruit and flowers to pantry  staples and organs. A team of around 70 trained data labelers in the US and overseas spend their days sniffing things and writing down what they smell like, using a standardized fragrance vocabulary.

Mapping out scents in this way is throwing out some unlikely parallels. In the same way that changing the order of words can drastically influence the meaning of a sentence, rearranging scent molecules in different proportions can drastically alter the smells humans perceive. “The scent tokens that define the smell of a newborn baby have massive overlap with the scent tokens in a fresh plate of cooked spaghetti,” Wiltschko says. (Specifically Barilla brand spaghetti, he says, which perhaps raises some questions for the people at the pasta factory.)

The company also creates its own scents, using a smell-printing robot the size of a school bus that mixes ingredients according to precise formulas to make samples for Osmo’s own research and fragrances for paying customers. It can design and print scents to order based on a ChatGPT-style prompt. Wiltschko flipped open his laptop to show me how the AI model worked. He opened a text box on screen, and I asked him to generate a fragrance that smelled like a Portuguese custard tart (we were in Lisbon for Web Summit), aimed at 18- to 23-year-old men. The system spent a few minutes cogitating, then generated three options for potential scent profiles that matched the brief (creamy, coconutty, fruity) and the molecules needed to create them. If I’d continued with the ordering process, my signature L’Eau de Custard would have been ready about a week later.

Osmo’s technology has already been used to create retail fragrances, including for giants like Procter & Gamble. The Gates Foundation, which invested $5 million when Osmo launched, later gave the company a $3.5 million grant to assess molecules that repel disease-carrying insects, and Osmo identified eight substances that were more repellent than DEET. Osmo has also worked with StockX, the online clothing marketplace, on using smell to spot counterfeit sneakers by detecting differences in the chemical composition of the materials used in the shoes.
